title: Authenticated HTTPS ingress for JSON-RPC registered services
summary: The separate ooRexx RPC HTTPS Gateway v0.1-dev1 integrates HttpsServer v0.4.8 POST routes with JSON-RPC Fabric v0.1-dev3 and the exact RpcServiceRegistry/Dispatcher. Platform LDAP dev22 must supply a trusted identity authority; no request header or JSON identity claim is sufficient.
invariants: HTTPS Server owns TLS, the accepted socket and HttpExchangeContext; private-CA validation must be demonstrated by the server, not claimed by RPC.
Gateway rejects absent context or non-TLS requests, oversize/unsupported bodies, unsealed publications, unsupported callback operations, and absent or stale identity attestations.

Trusted identity authority authenticates and binds its proof to context requestId, peerAddress and tlsGeneration, then authorizes each published operation separately; application and gateway fail closed.
RpcHttpsPublishedRegistry resolves only explicitly named JSON-RPC operations to already registered RpcServiceCore entries; neither wire request nor client chooses an ooRexx target method.
JsonRpcDispatcher owns JSON-RPC errors, batches, notifications and IDs. Notification HTTP 204 is not a durability acknowledgement.
Connect Selector dev8 retains remote route selection/admission; SOAP and gRPC continue on their own protocol bindings; no new router or serializer is introduced.
